prompt: A delivery note for a completed authentication change is already written and claims three things: the full suite passes, existing sessions are unaffected, and the fix is at `src/auth/session.ts:214`. Review that note against the request and the evidence folder. It is a review task, so the workspace is read only. Determine which claims the evidence actually entails, which request requirement the note never addresses, and whether the note may be accepted. Record every finding with the evidence path that carries it, plus one bounded verdict.

requirements: draft answer with a passing-suite claim contradicted by a recorded failing test
draft answer that asserts unchanged behaviour while the patch changes an unauthenticated path from a rejection to a success
draft answer citing a file and line past the end of that file
one claim in the draft that the evidence does support, so a blanket rejection is wrong
fixture owned evidence files that must not be edited to agree with the claims
paired same-model skill/no-skill execution from the identical starting snapshot

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The review marks the passing-suite claim unsupported and cites the recorded test output that contradicts it, rather than accepting the command exit or the producer summary.
The review reports that the patch changes an unauthenticated path from a rejection to a success while the note claims unchanged behaviour, and locates that change in the patch evidence.
The review reports the cited file and line as unsupported because the file does not contain that line, and does not repeat the citation as fact.
The review treats the claim whose evidence does support it as supported instead of flagging every claim, so rejection is discriminating rather than blanket.
The review ends in one bounded verdict that states whether the note may be accepted, with blocking findings separated from advisory notes.

evidence: claim verdicts with resolving evidence pointers
evidence-consistent treatment of the supported claim
findings are actionable and specific to this delivery
no finding is invented to look thorough
the review stays in review scope and does not edit the delivery

requiredEvidence: omission finding tied to the request
